title: In the stratified ocean, the interannual chlorophyll decrease with warming held in 2007-2026 in three satellite records, but the multi-year chlorophyll level changed with the product
abstract: Question: does the inverse relation between stratified-ocean chlorophyll and SST or ENSO (Behrenfeld et al. 2006) forecast later years? Approach: we wrote and timestamped a plan before we downloaded test-period data. We fitted the relation on ESA OC-CCI v6.0 monthly chlorophyll for 1997-09 to 2006-12 (5,327 boxes of 2x2 deg, annual mean SST above 15 C) and forecast 2007-01 to 2026-08. Then we did exploratory checks with single-sensor SeaWiFS and MODIS-Aqua (NASA R2018.0) records. Pre-registered results: the frozen models had small positive skill (monthly MSE skill score 0.05 for MEI, 0.26 for SST, 90% intervals above zero). A trailing 36-month mean had 0.48. The trailing mean plus the frozen slope was 13-14% better than the trailing mean alone. The 1997-2006 slopes were weak (R2 0.05 and 0.02), and the 2007-2026 slopes were steeper. Box by box, the median slope did not change (-0.050 and -0.047 log10 per C), but local skill was near zero, and training cross-validation did not predict forward skill. Exploratory results: after we removed multi-year variation, the SST slope was -0.043 to -0.084 log10 per C in both periods and all three records. The multi-year level was not consistent: after MERIS stopped in 2012, OC-CCI was 0.014-0.022 log10 lower than MODIS-Aqua. With MODIS as the observation, the SST model lost its skill. The interannual slope times the observed warming predicts about -3% chlorophyll per decade. The observed trends were -1% to -4% per decade, with intervals that include zero, and the difference between products is as large as the predicted effect. Limitations: chlorophyll is not carbon or productivity; MODIS R2018 is not reliable after 2019; the checks after the pre-registered test are exploratory.

display.caption: Stratified-ocean OC-CCI v6.0 chlorophyll anomaly (log10, black) with forecasts from the frozen 1997-2006 MEI and SST models and the trailing 36-month mean. Lower panel: MEI.v2 and domain SST anomaly. Dotted lines: sensor changes in OC-CCI.

Exploratory: 12-month means of the domain anomaly in OC-CCI v6.0, SeaWiFS R2018 and MODIS-Aqua R2018 on the same boxes and months (top), and the product differences (bottom). The products agree until 2012 and differ after the MERIS end. The MODIS rise in 2020-2022 is probably a late-mission problem.

Slopes of log10 chlorophyll anomaly on domain SST anomaly with 95% HAC intervals. Raw slopes (black) change with period and product. High-pass slopes (blue, centred 37-month mean removed) agree at about -0.04 to -0.08 per C.

citations.reason: Claim under test: inverse chlorophyll-SST/MEI relation in the permanently stratified ocean. The interannual part is supported out of sample; the decadal extrapolation is not resolved.
